_readme: Settings for run_engine_wrapper.py --limit-design burden. Every value is a PROPOSAL for Credit Risk to set. Keys starting with an underscore are comments and are ignored. Anything omitted falls back to the default in limit_design.py. The reasoning for each value is in the Credit Risk document.
_why_capacity_ceiling_multiple: Limit may not exceed this many months of the agent's commission (6-month commission / 6). Measured bad-loan rate is about 1.9% at 3-4x for borrowers with a clean streak and about 2.5% at 4-6x; 3x would cut total limits about 8%.
_why_keep_peak_season_haircut: Keeps the engine's 15% capacity cut in January, August, September and December. Not yet validated against outcomes; removing it adds about 2 points to the mean limit.
_why_engine_ceiling: Outer bound; matches the Bank of Uganda cap the engine already enforces. The product maximum is a separate decision for Product and Credit Risk.
_why_risk_base_limit: The risk cap is risk score x this value, so it must be raised with the ceiling or no limit can exceed 1,000,000. Raised alone it is NOT safe: see the governor.

governor._why: Any increase over what the 1,000,000-ceiling engine would give is limited to this multiple of the borrower's largest past loan. Without it, 23% of borrowers would be above 1,000,000 and the median limit would be 1.96x their largest past loan. 1.0x gives +11.8% total limits, 1.25x +19.3%, 1.5x +26.5% (versus the 1,000,000-ceiling version).

ladder._why: Multiples of monthly commission by experience. First loans: 0.29% bad at or below 2x versus 3.19% at 2-3x. One or two clean loans: thin evidence (61 bad loans in 4,190), set at 3x. Established with an on-time streak: 4x. Unknown outcome counts as not clean (conservative). Severe overdue = 30+ days past a loan's due date, the definition already used in the loan-state query.

arrears._why: 1-30 days overdue holds the borrower at 3x or below (no graduation); over 30 days or an open rollover drops to 2x. Blocking lending outright at 30+ days (963 borrowers holding 183M) is left OFF as a policy choice for Credit Risk.

_why_risk_tier_multipliers_apply_to_firs: Borrowers with no history get a default risk score of 0.63, so every first-exposure borrower is tier 2 or 3 (multiplier 0.85 or 0.65) on top of the 2x cap. Kept ON (conservative). Switching OFF adds about 4.7% to total limits.

pd._why_tier_pd_cutoffs: Used only for borrowers with a calibrated PD. The engine's cut-offs (0.85 / 0.60 / 0.35) were built for the 7-signal score; the calibrated PD tops out near 16%, so on (1 - PD) every borrower is tier 1 or 2. The PD is calibrated, so it reads as an expected bad-loan rate: tier 1 at or below the 2% appetite, tier 2 to 5%, tier 3 to 10%, tier 4 above 10%. Set to null to use the engine's own cut-offs.
pd._why_thin_file_definition: The PD model's thin-file flag means no loan history at all and flags only 20 of 9,603 thin-file borrowers; using it would remove the thin-file weights for borrowers with 1-2 loans. 'engine' keeps the engine's own definition (fewer than 3 loans).

_why_min_usable_loan: Smallest loan ever disbursed is about 300,000 (0.02% of loans are smaller). Used only to flag limits below it; it does not change any limit. To be confirmed by Product.
_candidate: S5 with the established ceiling at 3x (established streak 3x instead of 4x); everything else as S5. Conservative-appetite alternative to S5 (established at 4x). Run with --pd-artifacts-dir output\pd_artifacts_labelC_train20260531_val20260831 for the corrected-label PD.
